subject: Request: temporary route-priority exception & short-term mitigation for FinCrest latency spikes
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Runtime Team <runtime@redwood.com>, Product Team <product@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary route-priority exception & short-term mitigation for FinCrest latency spikes

Team —

Quick background: FinCrest (large payments customer, deal DL-2027-092) reported repeated tail-latency spikes this morning on our hosted API when they exercise high-concurrency embedding + chat requests. They run a routing strategy that pins to multi-variant models; spikes seem correlated with route selection and concurrent KV cache warms.

They're seeing 95th/99th percentiles jump ~3-4x during sustained bursts; Procurement is on the line and they're asking for a short-term SLA mitigation while we diagnose. They are open to a temporary config change on our side (route priority override or forced sticky routing to a stable variant) for the weekend to stabilize traffic.

Ask: can Runtime/Platform approve a temporary exception (route_hint_priority flag enabled for FinCrest only) + a quick mitigation plan we can offer (config + process) while Product decides longer-term API exposure?

What I need by EOD: a) whether we can enable an account-scoped route-priority override, b) suggested safe mitigation steps (config patch, canary window, rollback plan), c) estimated ETA for canary release if code change required.

I attached the logs FinCrest sent (fincrest_latency_logs.zip). Alicia copied below.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Runtime Team <runtime@redwood.com>, Product Team <product@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary route-priority exception & short-term mitigation for FinCrest latency spikes

Sean —

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. Quick triage notes:
- I spun up a repro on staging that mimics their concurrent embedding -> chat pattern; I can reproduce elevated tail-latency when variants are switching and KV cache warms overlap with large batch sizes.
- Short-term mitigation (safe, configuration-only): reduce batch size for affected route, enable sticky routing to the stable L3 variant, and temporarily turn off autoscaling burst for that tenant so we don't surface additional cold starts.

About the "route_hint_priority" concept: we don't currently expose account-scoped priority flags in the control plane. We have a kernel-level selector that can accept a per-request route_hint, but to make it account-scoped we'd need a small change to routing policy lookup (~1-2 PRs) and a canary pipeline. I estimate ~36-48 hours to get a canary out if we treat this as a runtime toggle behind a feature flag.

Immediate ask to Sales: can FinCrest accept a maintenance window (2 hours) where we can enable sticky routing + reduced batch size? That can be done today via config (no code change). If they want the account-scoped override persisted without manual ops, that's the 36-48h path.

I've opened RUNTIME-4567 and attached initial repro steps.
—Dev
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@fincrest.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary route-priority exception & short-term mitigation for FinCrest latency spikes

Sean —

Thanks for the quick response. We're seeing the errors escalate during batch runs that occur nightly between 02:00-03:30 UTC. The attached logs contain a couple of stack traces when a subset of requests timed out (see fincrest_error_snippet.txt inside the zip).

We can accept a maintenance window tonight (01:30-03:30 UTC). We'd prefer not to have any code change during that window — config changes are fine. If the temporary config stabilizes, procurement is willing to pause the SLO conversation while you ship a permanent solution.

—Alicia
FinCrest, Platform Ops
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary route-priority exception & short-term mitigation for FinCrest latency spikes

Following up with a playbook we can run for the maintenance window:

1) Pre-window (30m) — snapshot their config + disable autoscaling burst for tenant (ops only, zero code).
2) Enable sticky routing to variant L3 for account (config toggle on the router side).
3) Reduce default embedding batch_size to 4 for FinCrest (config).
4) Monitor 95/99 percentiles and error rates; if improvements plateau in 20 minutes, keep the config for the window.
5) If errors increase, rollback sticky routing and restore previous config.

I've prepared an SLA exemption template (SLA_exemption_template.pdf) for legal; if Product signs off on the longer-term exposure, we can convert the manual config into a gated feature flag (RUNTIME-4567).

Karthik — can you confirm the safety of enabling the sticky routing flag as a tenant-scoped config immediately, or does that risk cross-tenant cache pollution?

-Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary route-priority exception & short-term mitigation for FinCrest latency spikes

Marissa / team —

I ran the cache-isolation assessment quickly: enabling a tenant-scoped sticky routing entry is safe provided we also namespace the KV cache keys by tenant (we already do this for private deployments but not always for hosted multi-tenant variants). For a short-lived emergency window, I can add a small config guard that forces tenant-key namespacing and enable the sticky routing flag. That requires one low-risk runtime change and a gated deploy. ETA: I'll have a canary PR and deploy plan within ~36 hours from now. For tonight's window we should proceed with the config-only mitigation Marissa outlined (sticky routing via ops toggle + reduce batch size).

Sean — please confirm FinCrest approved the 01:30-03:30 UTC window and copy Procurement; I'll prepare the canary PR and link it to RUNTIME-4567. Also include a contact for on-call if we need to rollback mid-window.

-Karthik
